name: Kneebar Finish
description: Kneebar Finish after Carni requires a separate leg-lock setup. Release the shoulder clamp, then establish hip and ankle control before extending the knee.
conditions: The attacker has isolated one leg between the legs, with the opponent's knee aligned at the hip fulcrum and the ankle controlled.
Confirm control of the opponent's thigh and ankle before considering a knee-extension attack.
Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.
summary: The Kneebar is a straight leg lock that controls the hip and ankle while placing a fulcrum behind the knee, threatening knee extension when the attacker closes the hips.
overview:
The attacker has isolated one leg between the legs, with the opponent's knee aligned at the hip fulcrum and the ankle controlled. Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.

Confirm control of the opponent's thigh and ankle before considering a knee-extension attack. Use the legs to keep the opponent's hip from moving freely away. Place the knee at the hip fulcrum with the leg in a straight, non-twisted line.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Rob Biernacki — three leg-lock control points](https://www.grapplearts.com/three-critical-control-points-leglock/); [Richie Martinez — Carni shoulder lock from Z guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iClQ2Np-n30).

defender.overview:
The attacker has isolated one leg between the legs, with the opponent's knee aligned at the hip fulcrum and the ankle controlled. Carni is a shoulder-lock configuration. A kneebar needs a separately captured leg and a new hip-to-knee alignment; neither the Carni leg clamp nor its name supplies that alignment.

A knee trapped at the attacker's hips with the ankle held indicates the extension threat. Hand fight and keep the lower leg free before the attacker completes the capture. Move the knee away from the fulcrum only while the leg can still move freely.

Avoid a twisting escape against a held ankle and trapped thigh. Do not wait for severe pain or test how far the knee can bend backward. Rebuild guard or base once the whole leg has been freed.
